skill.description: Coordinate AI coding agents on a Kanban board with git worktree isolation, MCP setup guidance, and PR-oriented review.

skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed a critical Docker deployment risk from combining an unpinned container image with a host Docker socket mount. Additional confirmed risks include sourcing .env as shell code, persistent hidden agent configuration writes, secret-printing troubleshooting guidance, unpinned npx execution, and destructive cleanup behavior. Most Markdown backtick, localhost URL, loopback IP, and placeholder secret detections were false positives in documentation context.

remediation.issue: Docker Compose mounts the host Docker socket into the Vibe Kanban container.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the docker.sock volume mount or replace it with a narrowly scoped deployment mechanism that cannot control the host daemon.

remediation.issue: The Docker template uses an unpinned latest image.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the container image to a reviewed version or digest and document the update process before remote deployment.

remediation.issue: The start workflow runs an unpinned npm package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the Vibe Kanban package version, document the expected checksum or release, and require review before upgrades.

remediation.issue: The start script sources .env as shell code and troubleshooting guidance prints secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Parse .env as data only, reject shell syntax, and replace secret echo checks with redacted presence checks.

remediation.issue: MCP setup writes hidden Claude and Codex configuration files in the user home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Show an exact diff, create a backup, and require explicit confirmation before writing persistent agent configuration.

remediation.issue: The cleanup script can force-remove worktrees and delete branches.
remediation.suggestion: Make dry-run the default, require typed confirmation for deletion, and avoid parsing branch names from human-readable git output.

remediation.issue: Auto Approve is documented as enabled by default for agents.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend Auto Approve off by default and document when approvals are safe for trusted repositories only.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned npx Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly starts Vibe Kanban through npx without pinning a package version or checksum, including the executable start wrapper. This creates supply-chain risk because a future package release or dependency compromise would run in the user workspace.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command examples and start script directly invoke npx vibe-kanban without a pinned version. npx execution is legitimate for this tool but high impact because it runs external package code locally.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Docker Image with Host Docker Access
semantic_findings.description: The Docker template uses the latest Vibe Kanban image while also mounting the host Docker socket. A future or compromised image release would receive direct access to the host Docker daemon.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The compose file directly uses an unpinned latest image and mounts /var/run/docker.sock. The combination creates a clear supply-chain path to host-level control.

semantic_findings.title: Environment File Sourced as Shell Code
semantic_findings.description: The start script loads .env with shell source instead of parsing key-value pairs. A crafted .env can execute arbitrary shell commands before Vibe Kanban starts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 82 directly uses source .env, which executes shell syntax from the file. This is a clear code execution risk when .env content is untrusted or copied from another source.

semantic_findings.title: Auto-Approved Agent Actions Increase Blast Radius
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents Auto Approve as enabled by default for agents. In a board that launches coding agents in git worktrees, default approval can allow broad filesystem and command actions before human review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly states Auto Approve is on by default and the surrounding workflow runs agent CLIs against repositories. The exact runtime permissions depend on agent configuration, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Cleanup Script Can Force Delete Worktrees and Branches
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup helper identifies Vibe Kanban worktrees and can force-remove worktrees and delete branches. A parsing error or broad --all run can remove local work that has not been reviewed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script loops over detected worktrees and runs forced removal and branch deletion commands. It supports dry-run, but the destructive path is present and automated.

content.user_title: Coordinate AI Agents on a Kanban Board
content.value_statement: Parallel AI coding work is hard to track across branches, logs, and pull requests. This skill gives practical Vibe Kanban setup guidance for local boards, MCP connections, worktree isolation, and review flow.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to start Vibe Kanban locally with npx or the provided Bash wrapper.
Documents MCP setup for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode configuration files.
Describes workspace creation, agent assignment, git worktree isolation, and pull request review.
Provides scripts for local startup, MCP configuration, health checks, and worktree cleanup.
Includes Docker Compose deployment guidance for remote or team board usage.
Lists environment variables for ports, CORS, remote mode, and agent API keys.
limitations: Requires Node.js, git, Vibe Kanban, and the selected agent CLIs to be installed and authenticated.
Remote deployment examples need security review before use on shared networks.
Bash scripts assume a Unix-like shell and common tools such as curl, jq, and git.
Does not replace human review of agent changes, secrets handling, or pull request quality.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Feature Work
use_cases.description: Break an epic into independent Vibe Kanban workspaces, assign agents, and review each result as a separate branch or pull request.

use_cases.title: Compare Agent Implementations
use_cases.description: Run the same scoped task with different agents and compare diffs, logs, and test outcomes before choosing a direction.

use_cases.title: Prepare Local Agent Orchestration
use_cases.description: Set up local MCP connections, environment variables, and health checks so agent work can be monitored from one board.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Local Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Vibe Kanban skill to help me start a local board for this repository. Check prerequisites, choose a safe port, and explain what I should verify before creating a workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Workspaces for an Epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Vibe Kanban to split this feature into three independent workspaces. For each workspace, suggest a focused title, an agent choice, review evidence, and a pull request boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Configure MCP for Codex
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current setup and prepare Vibe Kanban MCP configuration for Codex. Show the files that would change and ask before writing hidden configuration files.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Remote Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the Vibe Kanban remote deployment plan for this team. Identify network exposure, secret handling, Docker risks, and safe alternatives before any deployment steps.

output_examples.input: Start Vibe Kanban for a repository on a non-default port.
output_examples.output: A concise checklist covering Node availability, selected port, local board URL, browser behavior, and agent authentication status.

output_examples.input: Plan three independent cards for a billing feature.
output_examples.output: Three scoped card titles with suggested agents, expected files or areas, review evidence, and pull request boundaries.

output_examples.input: Review stale Vibe Kanban worktrees before cleanup.
output_examples.output: A cleanup recommendation that separates clearly merged worktrees from branches requiring manual approval.

best_practices: Keep each Vibe Kanban card small enough to review as one pull request.
Review diffs, logs, and test results before moving agent work to Done or merging a pull request.
Keep remote mode, Docker deployment, and MCP config changes behind explicit human approval.
anti_patterns: Do not run multiple broad agents against the same files without worktree isolation.
Do not expose Vibe Kanban remote mode to untrusted networks with secrets loaded.
Do not mount host Docker socket or write hidden agent configs without security review.

faq.question: Does this skill install Vibe Kanban by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and scripts that use the external Vibe Kanban package and local agent CLIs.

faq.question: Which AI tools are covered?
faq.answer: The documentation covers Claude, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini, and several agents supported by Vibe Kanban.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: It describes the Vibe Kanban workflow for draft pull requests when GitHub integration is configured.

faq.question: Is remote deployment safe by default?
faq.answer: No. Remote mode, CORS, secrets, and Docker configuration should be reviewed before exposing a board.

faq.question: Does it protect API keys?
faq.answer: No. Users must manage API keys carefully and avoid printing them, storing them in unsafe files, or exposing them to untrusted containers.

faq.question: Can I use it without MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The board can be used through the browser UI, while MCP is optional agent integration.
